chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Preparing to replace Joe Thomas; the Lunceford drummer's bet
summary: McRae learned the Lunceford records beforehand, played the hard book and "Let's Keep Smiling", and won the drummer's bet.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Now I got to go out and take Joe Thomas' place. I know what Joe Thomas is playing in the band.
They're doing a thing called "Let's Keep Smiling"-- they're doing that. The Joe had recorded that and he was singing it -- the solo thing -- it was built around him like a show tune for him.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
When Jimmy Lunceford used to open a theater, that's where they featured Joe Thomas on. Open up a big introduction, play sixteen bars and modulate right into Joe --
And Joe walk down there and he's playing his thing, "Let's Keep Smiling," and singing it.
So now I got to go out and take his place. Here I go again.

So now, Jimmy Crawford and his drummer, you know -- Jimmy's a great -- he's a great drummer. He's telling Jimmy Lunceford that, "I bet he can't. I bet he can't. I bet he don't." Jimmy Lunceford say, "I bet he will." (Inaudible). "A bet." He say, "Okay, you want to bet, let's bet fifty dollars."
Then when I got there (inaudible) -- And during the time I'm coming out there they're arguing and got it up to a hundred dollars, you know.
You know, I don't know what's going on.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

So what I do, I go get the record on Let's Keep Smiling, and get three of Jimmy Lunceford's top things that he's got out that's really tough -- the saxophone things, you know. "Walking By The River," that chorus on the sax, that was really -- well now I'm playing it. So I say (inaudible). Joe Thomas (inaudible). He's gonna play second tenor. I'll get -- familiarize myself.
So I go and bought the records and sit down in a room -- back room and play it over and just familiarize myself with what was going on with his top things, with the rest of the stuff.
And learned the song, "Let's Keep Smiling", the way Joe Thomas play it, you know, (inaudible) the breaks he makes to come in so it'll make -- (inaudible) just like the record.

So I learned that. We're playing -- I met them somewhere in Akron. So now, we wanna go to the theater in Chicago, the same theater that I played with Ella and Chick, you know. We get to Fort Wayne, Indiana. Now we're playing -- I go out there and --
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

The first time I was with him out there in Akron, I played a book. Went out to the dance with them (inaudible) -- got dressed, went out to the dance with him and Joe said, 'I'm gonna take the first set down. After I take the first set down, you got it. I'm gone.'
So now they don't play -- I think that he's betting that I'm not gonna play in the second set that I'm gonna open up with.
Play that 'Walking By The River' thing. Other couple of things (inaudible). The reed section sound good, man.
Jimmy Lunceford say, 'Mr. Crawford.' 'Okay, I'll take it.' And he handed him over two hundred dollars.
I say, 'What is this?' He say, 'Now here's a hundred dollars for you and I got a hundred dollars.' He say, 'That he was betting me that you wouldn't play the book.'
After the thing was over, he say, 'Betting me you wouldn't (inaudible) don't play this book.' See, Joe had gone.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

Joe didn't even wait around. Joe had gone. Now when we get to Fort Wayne, Indiana coming into Chicago, Eddie Wilcox tells Jimmy -- says, "Why don't we keep (inaudible) -- Because they had played (inaudible) these numbers. This particular number here they hadn't played yet, because they figured that I didn't know this, you know. He says, "Why can't we play Let's Keep Smiling?" And whatchacallem say, "Oh, Teddy don't know that." Jimmie Lunceford say, 'Let's Keep Smiling. Ready for it, Teddy?' Because I had told Mr. Lunceford I had worked on it, I think I can do it, you know. So Wilcox say, "Why can't we play Let's Keep Smiling?" And Jimmie Lunceford say, "Let's Keep Smiling." Wilcox say, "Teddy can't play that." He say, "Don't worry about Teddy. Let's play (inaudible)."
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
They hit into that thing, man, and I walked down in front of that bandstand and Wilcox come up there, "(Inaudible) floor show. Mr. Floor-show."
When they got to Chicago, the first number they opened up with -- they (inaudible), I tore that theater up.
I tore that theater up because I had some other things. Jimmy Lunceford come off, say, (inaudible).

Wilcox say, "Mr Floorshow."
I say, "Well, I'm" --
"I tell you what I did. I was gonna let you guys" --
I say, "I'll tell you just what I did. I went home -- when you sent for me I went and got your record and I studied them for two days before I came out here -- before I left New York.
I say, "I won't let you guys pull nothing on me." They laughed.
Jimmy say, "I told you, you don't have to worry about him."
